rows.claim: God made the House secure and beyond the reach of rulers’ domination, so those who sought refuge there were safe despite fear around them.
rows.anchor: فجعل هذا البيت آمنا ، وجعله عتيقا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sanctuary’s protection continued even when people associated partners with God; its safety served a divine purpose.
rows.anchor: حتى حين انحرف الناس وأشركوا بربهم وعبدوا معه الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserved the sanctuary during the People of the Elephant attack; Quraysh’s secure sanctuary contrasted with people being seized nearby.
rows.anchor: ولما توجه أصحاب الفيل لهدمه كان من أمرهم ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh sanctuary is a safe enclave while people around it are taken away, a sign of God’s protection.
rows.anchor: أو لم يروا أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا ويتخطف الناس من حولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Elephant event magnified the House’s sanctity throughout Arabia and raised the standing of Quraysh, its people and custodians.
rows.anchor: وقد كان لحادث الفيل أثر مضاعف في زيادة حرمة البيت عند العرب في جميع أنحاء الجزيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elevated status of Quraysh let them travel with honor and care and establish major caravan routes to Yemen and Syria.
rows.anchor: مما ساعدهم على أن يسيروا في الأرض آمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh organized major seasonal caravans, traveling to Yemen in winter and Syria in summer.
rows.anchor: وشجعهم على إنشاء خطين عظيمين من خطوط التجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Arabia was insecure and raids were common, the House’s sanctity secured Quraysh’s lucrative trade and gave them a distinctive advantage and ample livelihood.
rows.anchor: فإن حرمة البيت في أنحاء الجزيرة قد كفلت لجيرته الأمن والسلامة في هذه التجارة المغرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two safe, profitable journeys became a familiar custom for Quraysh.
rows.anchor: وألفت نفوسهم هاتين الرحلتين الآمنتين الرابحتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the mission began, God reminded Quraysh of the Elephant deliverance, their habitual journeys, their provision, and their safety at home and on the road.
rows.anchor: هذه هي المنة التي يذكرهم الله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journeys brought plentiful food to people whose own land was barren, and their comfort was a gift from God.
rows.anchor: ومنة الرزق الذي أفاضه عليهم بهاتين الرحلتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s protection covered Quraysh both at home beside the House and while traveling under its sanctity.
rows.anchor: سواء في عقر دارهم بجوار بيت الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These favors should shame Quraysh for worshipping others alongside the Lord who keeps them safe and nourished and protects their journeys.
rows.anchor: يذكرهم بهذه المنن ليستحيوا مما هم فيه من عبادة غير الله معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In gratitude for the safe, familiar journeys, Quraysh are commanded to worship the Lord of the House who secured them.
rows.anchor: رحلة الشتاء والصيف فليعبدوا رب هذا البيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the condition of their land, hunger would have been expected, but God fed and satisfied them.
rows.anchor: فأطعمهم الله وأشبعهم من هذا الجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given Quraysh’s weakness and dangerous surroundings, fear would have been expected, but God made them secure.
rows.anchor: فآمنهم من هذا الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh knew the House’s value and, in crisis, appealed only to its Lord; Abd al-Muttalib told Abraha that he owned the camels but the House had a Lord to protect it.
rows.anchor: وها هو ذا عبد المطلب لا يواجه أبرهة بجيش ولا قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah Quraysh is independent and begins with the basmala, yet its placement after al-Fil fits their shared subject.
rows.anchor: وهذه السورة تبدو امتدادا لسورة الفيل قبلها من ناحية موضوعها وجوها

rows.speaker: الروايات
rows.claim: Reports say nine surahs separated the revelation of al-Fil and Quraysh; their consecutive order in the muṣḥaf still suits their related themes.
rows.anchor: والروايات تذكر أنه يفصل بين نزول سورة الفيل وسورة قريش تسع سور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ on dating: some call the whole surah Meccan, while others call its first three verses Meccan and the rest Medinan; Qutb calls the mixed account likelier.
rows.anchor: مكية مدنية في بعض الروايات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Qutb leans toward a wholly Medinan setting because hypocrisy and ostentation were unfamiliar in Mecca, he allows later verses to have been appended for thematic continuity.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت السورة كلها وحدة متماسكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven short verses overturn conventional ideas of faith and disbelief and reveal the creed’s mercy and immense good for humanity.
rows.anchor: إن هذه السورة الصغيرة ذات الآيات السبع القصيرة تعالج حقيقة ضخمة تكاد تبدل المفهوم السائد للإيمان والكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion is not outward forms or ritual; worship matters only when sincere devotion produces good deeds and sound social conduct.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الدين ليس دين مظاهر وطقوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religion is an integrated way of life whose worship, rites, and personal and social duties purify hearts and lead people to cooperation, care, and flourishing.
rows.anchor: إنما هو منهج متكامل ، تتعاون عباداته وشعائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verbal claim to Islam and performance of prayer or other rites do not prove faith; its signs must appear in the person’s conduct.
rows.anchor: ولقد يقول الإنسان بلسانه : إنه مسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith, once settled in the heart, immediately moves a person to righteous action; failure to move shows that faith is absent.
rows.anchor: إن حقيقة الإيمان حين تستقر في القلب تتحرك من فورها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question summons anyone able to see to identify the person who denies the Judgment.
rows.anchor: إنها تبدأ بهذا الاستفهام الذي يوجه كل من تتأتى منه الرؤية ليرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an answers who denies the Judgment by pointing to the person who shoves the orphan and refuses care for the poor, surprising under conventional definitions of faith.
rows.anchor: ومن هو هذا الذي يكذب بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes forcefully pushing the orphan, humiliating and harming the child.
rows.anchor: أي الذي يهين اليتيم ويؤذيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person neither urges food for the poor nor advises others to care for them.
rows.anchor: والذي لا يحض على طعام المسكين ولا يوصي برعايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If belief were genuine, the person would neither push the orphan away nor neglect urging food for the poor.
rows.anchor: وما كان ليقعد عن الحض على طعام المسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True assent transforms the heart and prompts kindness and care for fellow humans who need protection.
rows.anchor: إنما هي تحول في القلب يدفعه إلى الخير والبر بإخوانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God asks for deeds that confirm words; words without confirming action are worthless before Him.
rows.anchor: إنما يريد منهم معها أعمالا تصدقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These opening verses state with unusual clarity the spirit of the creed and the nature of the religion.
rows.anchor: وليس أصرح من هذه الآيات الثلاث في تقرير هذه الحقيقة التي تمثل روح هذه العقيدة وطبيعة هذا الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb declines to debate juristic boundaries of faith and Islam: those govern legal transactions, while this surah states God’s measure of the underlying reality.
rows.anchor: فأما هنا فالسورة تقرر حقيقة الأمر في اعتبار الله وميزانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning of ruin applies to people who are heedless of their prayer.
rows.anchor: إنه دعاء أو وعيد بالهلاك للمصلين الذين هم عن صلاتهم ساهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those heedless worshippers are the ones who show off and withhold small acts of help.
rows.anchor: إنهم ( الذين يراءون ويمنعون الماعون )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They perform prayer but fail to establish it.
rows.anchor: إنهم أولئك الذين يصلون ، ولكنهم لا يقيمون الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They carry out prayer’s movements and recite its supplications, but their hearts and spirits do not experience its recitations, prayers, or glorifications.
rows.anchor: وأرواحهم لا تستحضر حقيقة الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They pray for people’s approval instead of sincerely for God, so they remain heedless of the prayer they are performing.
rows.anchor: إنهم يصلون رياء للناس لا إخلاصا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The required act is establishing prayer, which requires conscious presence and standing before God alone.
rows.anchor: وإقامتها لا تكون إلا باستحضار حقيقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This surah, like al-Duḥā and al-Sharḥ, is addressed specifically to the Prophet: God consoles him, promises good, warns his enemies, and directs him to gratitude.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة خالصة لرسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah reflects the early Meccan life of the mission, including hostility toward the Prophet and God’s direct care and reassurance for him and the believers.
rows.anchor: وحياة الداعية في أول العهد بمكة

rows.speaker: سفهاء قريش
rows.claim: Quraysh scoffers, including al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, Abū Lahab, and Abū Jahl, mocked the Prophet as cut off because his sons had died.
rows.anchor: ورد أن سفهاء قريش ممن كانوا يتابعون الرسول

rows.speaker: أحدهم
rows.claim: One critic said the Prophet should be left alone, since he would die without descendants and his cause would end.
rows.anchor: وقال أحدهم : دعوه فإنه سيموت بلا عقب وينتهي أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The taunt resonated in a society that valued many sons and may have wounded the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا اللون من الكيد اللئيم الصغير يجد له في البيئة العربية التي تتكاثر بالأبناء صدى ووقعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah consoles the Prophet by affirming that his good will endure and his enemies will be cut off.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم نزلت هذه السورة تمسح على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kawthar is an unrestricted form of abundance, directly reversing the enemies’ claim that the Prophet was cut off.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى عكس المعنى الذي أطلقه هؤلاء السفهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abundant gift includes prophethood and communion with the ultimate reality, so whoever finds God has lost nothing.
rows.anchor: في هذا الاتصال بالحق الكبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an itself is an inexhaustible spring of abundant good given to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وسورة واحدة منه كوثر لا نهاية لكثرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavenly assembly blesses the Prophet, whose name is joined to God’s name in heaven and on earth.
rows.anchor: وهو واجده في الملأ الأعلى الذي يصلي عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s Sunnah has spread across the world through centuries, with millions following him, naming him, and loving his memory.
rows.anchor: وهو واجده في سنته الممتدة على مدار القرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good flowed to all generations through the Prophet, including people who never recognized or believed in its source.
rows.anchor: وهو واجده في الخير الكثير الذي فاض على البشرية في جميع أجيالها بسببه وعن طريقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifestations of this abundance cannot be exhaustively counted; leaving the gift undefined allows it to encompass every increase of good.
rows.anchor: إنه الكوثر ، الذي لا نهاية لفيضه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Reports through many routes identify al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise, while Ibn ʿAbbās says that river is only one part of the abundant good given to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ولكن ابن عباس أجاب بأن هذا النهر هو من بين الخير الكثير الذي أوتيه الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading of the Paradise river as one part of al-Kawthar best fits this context and its circumstances.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأنسب في هذا السياق وفي هذه الملابسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After affirming abundant favor, God directs the Prophet to answer provocation and plotting with gratitude through exclusive devotion in worship, prayer, and sacrifice.
rows.anchor: إلى شكر النعمة بحقها الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and sacrificial slaughter must be for God alone, without joining the polytheists’ worship or invoking another name over sacrifices.
rows.anchor: في الصلاة وفي ذبح النسك خالصا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated emphasis on God’s name alone over sacrifices and rejection of offerings dedicated to others shows Islam’s effort to remove shirk from every part of life.
rows.anchor: وفي تكرار الإشارة إلى ذكر اسم الله وحده على الذبائح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam is a religion of unity and pure monotheism that pursues shirk in all its visible and hidden forms.
rows.anchor: فهو دين الوحدة بكل معنى من معانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because life is one whole, Islam purifies both inward belief and outward practices and directs all of life to God alone.
rows.anchor: فالحياة وحدة ما ظهر منها وما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse says the Prophet is the possessor of abundant good, not the one cut off; this verse assigns that fate to his haters.
rows.anchor: في الآية الأولى قرر أنه ليس أبتر بل هو صاحب الكوثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s warning came true: the enemies’ names disappeared while Muhammad’s name spread and rose.
rows.anchor: ولقد صدق فيهم وعيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith, truth, and good have deep roots and wide branches; disbelief, falsehood, and evil are what become cut off.
rows.anchor: إن الإيمان والحق والخير لا يمكن أن يكون أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human measures mislead people about what lasts, but the lasting example disproves the critics’ claim.
rows.anchor: إن مقاييس الله غير مقاييس البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A call to God, truth, and good cannot be severed because it is joined to the living, everlasting God.
rows.anchor: إن الدعوة إلى الله والحق والخير لا يمكن أن تكون بتراء ولا أن يكون صاحبها أبتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs did not deny God, but failed to recognize Him as uniquely One and Self-Sufficient; they associated Him with idols representing ancestors, righteous people, or angels, and alleged kinship between God, angels, and jinn.
rows.anchor: لم يكن العرب يجحدون الله ولكن كانوا لا يعرفونه بحقيقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They treated idols as intermediaries, claiming they worshipped them only to bring them nearer to God.
rows.anchor: كما حكى عنهم القرآن الكريم في سورة الزمر قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They acknowledged God as creator and as the one who governs the sun and moon and sends rain, and used His name in oaths and supplication.
rows.anchor: ولقد حكى القرآن عنهم أنهم كانوا يعترفون بخلق الله للسماوات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite that acknowledgment, shirk distorted their beliefs and customs: they allotted crops, livestock, and children to false gods, sometimes sacrificing their children, as the Qur’an recounts.
rows.anchor: ولكنهم مع إيمانهم بالله كان هذا الشرك يفسد عليهم تصورهم كما كان يفسد عليهم تقاليدهم وشعائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claimed Abraham’s religion and thought themselves better guided than Jews and Christians, reasoning that angels and jinn were closer to God than Ezra or Jesus; Qutb says all such association is shirk.
rows.anchor: وكانوا يعتقدون أنهم على دين إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muhammad said his religion was Abraham’s, Quraysh asked why they should leave their way and follow him, then offered mutual prostration and a deal to stop criticizing their gods.
rows.anchor: إن دينه هو دين إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they acknowledged God while worshipping other beings, Quraysh thought a compromise or division of worship might bridge the gap with Muhammad.
rows.anchor: واعترافهم بالله مع عبادة آلهة أخرى معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah decisively ends the proposed bargain, distinguishing worship, method, worldview, and path through categorical and repeated negation.
rows.anchor: والمفاصلة الحاسمة بين عبادة وعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to say this is God’s decisive order: the creed belongs to God, who commands and rules without appeal.
rows.anchor: فهو الأمر الإلهي الحاسم الموحي بأن أمر هذه العقيدة أمر الله وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them disbelievers names their actual status: they are neither people of the true religion nor believers, so there is no shared path.
rows.anchor: وليسوا بمؤمنين وإنما هم كافرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s worship and object of worship differ from those of the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: فعبادتي غير عبادتكم ، ومعبودي غير معبودكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers’ worship and object of worship differ from Muhammad’s.
rows.anchor: فعبادتكم غير عبادتي ، ومعبودكم غير معبودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal sentence restates the first negation and signals that this distinction is stable and continuous.
rows.anchor: توكيد للفقرة الأولى في صيغة الجملة الإسمية وهي أدل على ثبات الصفة واستمرارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the second negation removes any remaining possibility of doubt through reiterated denial and emphasis.
rows.anchor: كي لا تبقي مظنة ولا شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing formula summarizes a complete separation: the two sides’ religions do not meet, resemble, connect, or mix.
rows.anchor: ثم إجمال لحقيقة الافتراق الذي لا التقاء فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Monotheism is a comprehensive method that directs people to God alone as the source of belief, law, values, standards, manners, morals, and their whole outlook on life.
rows.anchor: ويحدد الجهة التي يتلقى منها الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clear distinction is necessary both for the caller and for those being called.
rows.anchor: هذه المفاصلة بهذا الوضوح ضرورية للداعية . وضرورية للمدعوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Communities that once knew religion but later deviated can be harder to call than communities that never knew it, since they assume they are guided and their mixture of good and corrupt can tempt a preacher to compromise.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجماعات هي أعصى الجماعات على الإيمان في صورته المجردة من الغبش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is to leave all of pre-Islamic ignorance for Islam as a whole; monotheism and shirk are separate methods that cannot meet halfway.
rows.anchor: والسبيل هو الخروج عن الجاهلية بجملتها إلى الإسلام بجملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A caller must inwardly distinguish himself from ignorance in belief, method, and action, without meeting its people halfway; cooperation requires their full move to Islam.
rows.anchor: وأول خطوة في الطريق هي تميز الداعية وشعوره بالانعزال التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There can be no patching or partial solution, however much pre-Islamic ignorance dresses itself in Islamic language.
rows.anchor: ولا التقاء في منتصف الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The caller must understand that the two sides have different religions and paths and guide others toward his own without concession.
rows.anchor: وتميز هذه الصورة في شعور الداعية هو حجر الأساس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb says contemporary callers urgently need full repudiation, separation, and decisive clarity.
rows.anchor: وما أحوج الداعين إلى الإسلام اليوم إلى هذه البراءة وهذه المفاصلة وهذا الحسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb invokes the warning that hearts hardened after time passed and many became defiant, as a description of communities that previously knew revelation.
rows.anchor: فقست قلوبهم وكثير منهم فاسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call must begin as it did at first: among ignorance, with full distinction and no half-measures or patchwork.
rows.anchor: والتميز الكامل عن الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The religion announced here is pure monotheism, receiving all its outlook, values, creed, and law from God alone in every aspect of life.
rows.anchor: التوحيد الخالص الذي يتلقى تصوراته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without decisive clarity the message remains blurred and accommodating; the call can stand only on firmness, candor, courage, and clarity.
rows.anchor: إنها لا تقوم إلا على الحسم والصراحة والشجاعة والوضوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah promises God’s victory, the conquest, and mass entry into Islam, then directs the Prophet to glorify, praise, and seek forgiveness when these signs arrive.
rows.anchor: بنصر الله والفتح ودخول الناس في دين الله أفواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah also displays the creed’s goal of raising humanity toward honor, devotion, freedom, and release, a height reached under Islam.
rows.anchor: تكشف في الوقت ذاته عن طبيعة هذه العقيدة وحقيقة هذا المنهج

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that late in his life the Prophet often said tasbih, praise, repentance, and seeking forgiveness; he said God had shown him the sign in his community and commanded this response. Aḥmad narrates it, and Muslim gives the same wording.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : كان رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr identifies the conquest as Mecca’s conquest and says Arab tribes waited to see whether Muhammad would prevail before converting; within two years most of Arabia had accepted Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير في التفسير : والمراد بالفتح ها هنا فتح مكة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن سلمة
rows.claim: A report in al-Bukhārī says that when Mecca was conquered, tribes hurried to bring their Islam to the Prophet, corroborating their earlier waiting.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن سلمة قال : لما كان الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future-event reading matches the surah’s surface wording: the conquest and mass conversions are signs still to come, followed by a direction for the Prophet when they occur.
rows.anchor: فهذه الرواية هي التي تتفق مع ظاهر النص في السورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In al-Bukhārī’s report, ʿUmar asked Badr veterans about the surah and brought Ibn ʿAbbās into their discussion.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان عمر يدخلني مع أشياخ بدر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some of the elders understood the command as telling believers to praise God and seek forgiveness when given victory.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم : أمرنا أن نحمد الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interpreted the conquest as the sign of the Prophet’s approaching death, an interpretation ʿUmar said he also knew.
rows.anchor: فقال لي : أكذلك تقول يا بن عباس

rows.speaker: عمر ابن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar affirmed that Ibn ʿAbbās’s interpretation was the one he knew from the surah; al-Bukhārī alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر ابن الخطاب : لا أعلم منها إلا ما تقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Aisha report can be reconciled with Ibn ʿAbbās’s reading: once he saw the sign, the Prophet understood that his earthly duty was complete and his meeting with God near.
rows.anchor: حين رأى علامة ربه أدرك أن واجبه في الأرض قد كمل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that after the surah came down the Prophet told Fāṭima his own death had been announced; she first wept, then smiled when he said she would be the first of his family to join him.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس كذلك : قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If that report places revelation after the sign was already present, the Prophet would have recognized his approaching death when the surah matched the event.
rows.anchor: ففي هذا الحديث تحديد لنزول السورة

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: Umm Salama reports that at the conquest the Prophet privately told Fāṭima he would die, making her cry, then said she would be the foremost woman of Paradise after Mary, making her smile; al-Tirmidhī transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن أم سلمة - رضي الله عنها - قالت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qutb favors the reading that fits the Qur’anic wording and Aisha’s report: the conquest was the sign, after which the Prophet understood his meeting with God was near.
rows.anchor: فهذه الرواية تتفق مع ظاهر النص القرآني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s durable teaching is that events in the world happen by God’s timing, in His chosen form, and for His purpose.
rows.anchor: في مطلع الآية الأولى من السورة إيحاء معين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory is God’s act; neither the Prophet nor his companions control it, earn it as personal credit, or gain a personal share from it.
rows.anchor: فهو نصر الله يجيء به الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and believers serve only as people through whose hands God may bring victory and as its guardians and trustees.
rows.anchor: أن يجريه الله على أيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet and believers’ entire share in victory, conquest, and mass conversion is to serve as God’s guardians and trustees in what He brings about.
rows.anchor: هذا هو كل حظهم من النصر ومن الفتح ومن دخول الناس في دين الله أفواجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to God’s honor and victory through them, the Prophet and believers should turn to Him with glorification, praise, and seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: هو الإتجاه إلى الله بالتسبيح وبالحمد والاستغفار في لحظة الانتصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They praise God for entrusting them with His call and protecting His religion, and for showing mercy to humanity through Islam’s victory and mass conversion.
rows.anchor: التسبيح والحمد على ما أولاهم من منة بأن جعلهم أمناء على دعوته حراسا لدينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking forgiveness guards against pride and triumphal intoxication after a long struggle and hardship.
rows.anchor: الاستغفار من الزهو الذي قد يساور القلب أو يتدسس إليه من سكرة النصر بعد طول الكفاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also seeks pardon for impatience, distress, or wavering during hardship while waiting for God’s promised victory.
rows.anchor: والاستغفار مما قد يكون ساور القلب أو تدسس إليه في فترة الكفاح الطويل والعناء القاسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It asks pardon for failing to praise and thank God adequately, since human effort is limited while divine favors continually overflow.
rows.anchor: والاستغفار من التقصير في حمد الله وشكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the moment of triumph, seeking forgiveness reminds the soul of its weakness and failure, restraining pride and conceit.
rows.anchor: فأولى أن تطامن من كبريائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This sense of shortcoming restrains victors from tyrannizing conquered people, because authority and victory ultimately belong to God.
rows.anchor: ثم إن ذلك الشعور بالنقص والعجز والتقصير والإتجاه إلى الله طلبا للعفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended horizon makes human beings greater by humbling themselves before God and freeing the spirit from self-interest.
rows.anchor: الأفق الذي يكبر فيه الإنسان لأنه يطامن من كبريائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human liberation requires release from ego, desires, and appetites so that even victory is used to remember God alone.
rows.anchor: وعبثا يحاول الإنسان الانطلاق والتحرر وهو مشدود إلى ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the prophetic ethic that the Qur’an calls humanity to emulate.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الأدب الذي اتسمت به النبوة دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph responded to the fulfilled dream and family reunion by crediting God’s care and acknowledging His wisdom.
rows.anchor: يا أبت هذا تأويل رؤياي من قبل قد جعلها ربي حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even at the height of power and reunion, Joseph’s prayer makes submission and joining the righteous his final concern.
rows.anchor: رب قد آتيتني من الملك وعلمتني من تأويل الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Solomon saw the Queen of Sheba’s throne before him, he credited it to God’s favor and treated it as a test of gratitude.
rows.anchor: فلما رآه مستقرا عنده قال : هذا من فضل ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God granted the victory sign, Muhammad entered Mecca bowed in gratitude, though it had expelled and fought him, and he praised and sought forgiveness as taught.
rows.anchor: انحنى لله شاكرا على ظهر دابته ودخل مكة في هذه الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say the Prophet increased his glorification, praise, and seeking forgiveness after the conquest; this practice became his companions’ way as well.
rows.anchor: وجعل يكثر من التسبيح والحمد والاستغفار كما وردت بذلك الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith raises humanity toward clarity, strength, freedom, and spiritual vitality.
rows.anchor: وهكذا أشرقت وشفت ورفرفت
